headline: Lula’s Victory in Brazil Is a Defeat for Trumpism
summary: Opinion: in Brazil, Lula beat far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro on Oct. 25 to take a record fourth presidential term, a result the writer reads as a setback for Trump-style politics.

headline: Who Are the Houthis and Why Are They Attacking Saudi Arabia’s Airports?
summary: Explainer on Yemen's Houthi rebels as they step up attacks on Saudi airports and energy targets, including a Riyadh airport strike that killed 13 and delayed an EU-Gulf summit.

headline: What Early Voting Data Is Showing About the Midterm Elections
summary: Nearly 33 million Americans have already voted before the Nov. 3 midterms; registered Democrats make up more of the early ballots so far, but Republicans usually catch up on Election Day.

headline: What Trump’s Waiver of New Russia Sanctions Means for Ukraine
summary: Trump signed an executive order waiving many penalties under a law sanctioning Russia and Iran, angering lawmakers in both parties; the piece weighs what the move means for Ukraine.

headline: The Rise of Electrostates Could Redraw The Global Economy
summary: A scorecard of 16 economies finds the switch to electric power uneven: in most countries policy is moving faster than real-world rollout, which could reshape who leads the global economy.

headline: Trump Keeps Promising Cash on the Campaign Trail
summary: On the midterm trail Trump keeps promising Americans direct payments, including a $5,000 dividend TIME estimates would cost about $1.2 trillion, while earlier promised checks never arrived.

headline: We Won't Know the Answers to AI's Most Important Questions Until It's Too Late
summary: Former OpenAI and DeepMind researcher Geoffrey Irving puts the chance that smarter-than-human AI kills everyone at roughly 50%, admits the figure is rough, and warns the answers may come too late.

headline: AI Colonies Are Coming
summary: Opinion: Noah Giansiracusa argues that teams of AI agents working together matter more than any single model, citing OpenAI's claim that an agent swarm solved a Navier-Stokes problem.

headline: Nobel Prizes: What to Know About 2026's Winners
summary: Roundup of the 2026 Nobel Prizes: optogenetics pioneers who steer brain cells with light, physicist Francis Halzen for neutrino research, and chemists explaining why molecules have a 'handedness'.

headline: How a Fake Pollster May Have Hurt Real Candidates
summary: A pollster called Wedgewood admitted its surveys used made-up data as a stunt; outlets had cited its numbers, and Michigan Senate hopeful Mallory McMorrow says a fake poll helped dry up her donations.

headline: Now Is the Best Time to Get Your Flu Shot
summary: An epidemiologist says this year's flu wave may come early, so getting a shot now makes sense; a new mRNA flu vaccine, mFlusiva, is approved for people 50 and older.

headline: Trump Is Promising Health Care Checks Before the Midterms. How Far Will They Go?
summary: Before the midterms Trump is promising health-care checks, including a one-time $90 rebate to help older Americans with Medicare Part B premiums; the piece asks how far the money goes.

headline: Climate Change Is Accelerating Faster Than We Can Respond, Scientists Warn
summary: A 'State of the Climate' study in the journal BioScience finds seven of 16 planetary vital signs at record extremes and warns Earth could pass 2°C of warming before 2050.

headline: Five Facts You Need To Know From The U.N.'s Major Emissions Gap Report
summary: The UN's 2026 Emissions Gap report finds the 1.5°C target all but lost, with current policies heading for roughly 2.8°C of warming by 2100; TIME lists five takeaways.

summary: Honorees of TIME's new TIME100 Art list, among them Alicia Keys, Amy Sherald and Ken Griffin, gathered at a New York dinner to talk about influence, inspiration and collecting.

headline: Breaking Down the Emotional Ending of 'Four Hands, Two Sonatas'
query: TIME culture, arts and entertainment October 2026
summary: TIME unpacks the finale of the Korean drama 'Four Hands, Two Sonatas', where a doctor exposes the risky injection behind one lead's lie and the pair reunite three years later.

headline: Trump Administration Mounts ‘Largest Denaturalization Effort in Modern History’
summary: Trump's Justice Department moved to revoke the US citizenship of 40 naturalized people, billing it as the biggest denaturalization drive in modern history, a warning sign for naturalized citizens.

headline: Exclusive: Documents Show How Israel Steered Qatari Payments to Gaza
summary: Documents obtained by TIME suggest Israel had a larger hand in routing Qatar's payments into Gaza than Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has admitted.

headline: Mbappé Apologizes After ‘Dictator’ Mao Comment: What to Know
summary: French soccer star Kylian Mbappé apologized after his remark calling Mao Zedong a 'dictator' set off a backlash in China, where dairy giant Mengniu and other sponsors cut ties.

headline: I've Been Disabled Since I Was a Child. Co-Writing 'Being Heumann' Still Taught Me So Much
summary: Rebekah Taussig, a disabled co-writer of Netflix's 'Being Heumann' about the 1977 San Francisco disability sit-in, says the script showed what she owes those activists and warns a Justice Department memo guts their law.

headline: Exclusive: The Former General Who Could End the Netanyahu Era
summary: In an exclusive interview, ex-general Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main challenger in Israel's election, promises a state inquiry into the failures of Oct. 7 within two weeks of taking power.

headline: Labor Rights Activist Dolores Huerta Dies at 96. Here's What To Know About Her Trailblazing Life
summary: Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers union, has died at 96 in Bakersfield, California; TIME looks back on a life spent organizing for farmworkers' rights.

headline: As Israelis Await Final Election Results, Netanyahu and Rival Face Tough Path to Power

summary: With Israel's Oct. 27 election results still being counted, neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor ex-general Gadi Eisenkot looks set to win a Knesset majority, pointing to hard coalition talks.

headline: El Niño Is Bringing Kelvin Waves to California. Here's What To Know
query: TIME storm, flood, wildfire or earthquake October 2026
summary: TIME explains how El Niño is sending Kelvin waves toward California, where a state emergency is in place and storms on high tides could worsen erosion and flooding in towns like Malibu.

headline: Pawan Kumar Chandana Is on the 2026 TIME100 Next
summary: TIME100 Next profile of Pawan Kumar Chandana, ex-ISRO engineer and CEO of Hyderabad's Skyroot Aerospace, whose Vikram-1 became India's first private rocket to put customer satellites in orbit in July.

headline: Skye Duncan Is on the 2026 TIME100 Next
summary: TIME100 Next profile of Skye Duncan of the Global Designing Cities Initiative, whose team built a mirror box showing adults streets at a child's height; its design guide is backed by 130-plus cities and groups.
